signals.title: ERA-Fathom/fathom
signals.content: Catch the step where an AI agent contradicts a decision it already made, and read how much functional life the run has left (the expiry read). Adapters and a CLI for the Fathom committed-state read and expiry read over LangGraph, CrewAI, Letta, OpenInference, DBOS, and coding-agent traces.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: ERA-Fathom/fathom
Summary: This brief outlines recent observations on the Fathom AI framework. Analysts noted a recurring pattern where an AI agent reverses a previously made decision, exposing a potential inconsistency in its state management. The framework also provides a read‑only interface to query the remaining functional lifespan of a run (the “expiry read”). Current adapters and a command‑line interface (CLI) enable these reads across multiple orchestration layers, including LangGraph, CrewAI, Letta, OpenInference, DBOS, and coding‑agent trace logs. The capability is primarily OSINT‑relevant for monitoring AI operational health and detecting decision drift, but further validation is required to assess reliability and coverage.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: ERA-Fathom/fathom
ملخص: يوضح هذا الملخص الملاحظات الأخيرة حول إطار عمل Fathom للذكاء الاصطناعي. لاحظ المحللون نمطًا متكررًا حيث يعكس وكيل الذكاء الاصطناعي قرارًا سبق اتخاذه، ما يكشف عن احتمال وجود عدم اتساق في إدارة حالته. يوفر الإطار أيضًا واجهة قراءة فقط لاستعلام العمر الوظيفي المتبقي لتشغيل معين ("قراءة الانتهاء"). تم تطوير محولات وواجهة سطر أوامر (CLI) لتمكين هذه القراءات عبر عدة طبقات تنسيق، بما في ذلك LangGraph وCrewAI وLetta وOpenInference وDBOS وسجلات تتبع وكيل البرمجة. هذه القدرة ذات صلة بالـ OSINT لمراقبة صحة تشغيل الذكاء الاصطناعي واكتشاف انحراف القرارات، لكن يلزم مزيد من التحقق لتقييم موثوقيتها ونطاق تغطيتها.

signals.title: @IntEngineering: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink made the first public US government acknowledgement on Monday that the United States has placed "space contro
signals.content: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink made the first public US government acknowledgement on Monday that the United States has placed "space control weapons" in orbit, stating: "The United States now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action." Meink offered no details about the weapons' nature, quantity, or when they were deployed, citing deterrence as the only reason for the disclosure. Analysts speculate the weapons could include space-based jammers, laser dazzlers, or other non-kinetic systems — technologies that already exist at scale in orbit and would not generate the space debris associated with kinetic weapons. The announcement comes after years of US officials raising alarms about Russia and China's own space weapons programs: Russia deployed apparent anti-satellite weapons in orbit in 2020, and China routinely maneuvers satellites close to US military assets. "Is there any question about whether China or Russia have been developing these sorts of weapons?" Meink said. "For over a decade, we've expressed concern. We need to make sure we can protect ourselves." Analysts noted the vagueness of the statement limits its deterrent value. "It is too vague to have meaningful deterrent value," said Clayton Swope of the Center for Strategic and International Studies. The disclosure marks a significant shift in Pentagon openness about orbital warfare — and effectively confirms a weapons race in space is already underway. 📷 Getty Images
